messages:
olivia: Quick follow-up from the Sable Systems PM: postmortem summary (VPC peering BGP flap + on‑prem NIC flapping) is up: https://redwood.internal/pm/sable-2026. I'm collecting owners & ETAs for the remediation action items. Please reply with "owner — ETA — short note" so I can populate the tracker.

ashok: I'll own the VPC peering config audit — ETA Fri EOD. I'll run the peering-test job and paste the results here.

marcus: I'll take the on‑prem NIC driver/config work with Sable's infra team. Need them to approve a maintenance window; if approved I can do a rolling driver update and NIC stress test by next Tue.

kate: I'll triage the isolation bug seen during failover (replica dropped from cluster). Need logs from target window — @devex-bot can you pull the curated bundle for 2026-06-15 02:10–02:40 UTC?

devex-bot: Logs bundle ready: https://files.redwood.internal/sable/logs/sable-2026-06-15-0210-0240.tar.gz — includes system logs, dmesg, and l3 peering traces. :robot_face:

marcus: Thanks. Sable also asked for a rollback plan for the kernel/driver change. Draft runbook snippet I'm putting in the tracker:
```
# Rollback kernel-driver (quick rollback)
1. Coordinate maintenance window with Sable (30m).
2. sudo dpkg -r nx-driver-new && sudo apt-get install nx-driver-old
3. systemctl restart networking
4. Run NIC sanity: /usr/local/bin/nic-healthcheck --stress 1h
5. Confirm replicas rejoin cluster
```

olivia: Tracker (please add rows): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1sable-actions (columns: owner | item | priority | ETA | status | notes). I'll do a sync next Wed 09:00 PT to review blockers.

ashok: One more note — we're seeing a recurring pattern: three peering BGP flaps in the last 6 weeks across dedicated customers. I propose creating a recurring "peering health" task and a detection alert for session resets. @jordan can you own the detection and alerting?

jordan: Yep — will add metric for bgp.session.resets (per-peer 5m rate) and a pager threshold (>=3 resets in 10m). ETA Thu.

kate: Isolation bug: initial hypothesis — race between failover orchestration and iptables cleanup step causing transient blackhole. Repro sketch:
```
1) Start failover (promote replica B)
2) Immediately run cleanup script that removes iptables rules on replica A
3) Replica B not fully up; packets get dropped for 20–60s
```
I'll try to reproduce in staging and open a short PR to delay cleanup until health check passes.

incident-bot: Postmortem created and linked to incident RID-2026-1447 — assignees updated.

olivia: Thanks all. Quick ask — mark P1/P2 in tracker. If anything is P1 I'll escalate to eng-ops and loop in SRE. :thumbsup: 

marcus: +1

ashok: +1

jordan: +1

kate: I'll post updates here when I have repro steps and the PR. Tag me for merge approvals, @olivia.

olivia: Great — leaving this thread as the single source for updates. If anything slips beyond ETA, ping me directly.
